lessons.title: What's the Weather Like?
lessons.changes: Shortened and simplified for independent kindergarten reading; kept Annie's letter frame; removed the map, polar and rainforest sections; comprehension questions rewritten as choices with text evidence.

passage.title: What's the Weather Like?
passage.text: Dear Kindergartners, Hello! My name is Annie. I live in a big city called Washington, D.C. I will be your weather pen pal. There are many kinds of weather. It can be sunny, cloudy, windy, rainy, or stormy. The weather changes day by day. There are four seasons in a year: winter, spring, summer, and autumn. Winter is the coldest season. In spring, new plants grow and flowers bloom. Summer is the hottest season. In autumn, the leaves fall from the trees. Autumn is also called fall. The seasons always change in the same order, year after year. This is called a cycle. Your friend, Annie

passage.title: Winter
passage.text: Dear Kindergartners, Today I will tell you about winter. Winter is the coldest season of the year. Winter includes December, January, and February. A thermometer tells us how hot or cold it is. When it is cold, the liquid in the thermometer stays down low. In winter, people wear hats, mittens, and scarves to stay warm. When it is very cold, rain can turn into snow. I love to build snowmen and go sledding! Winter has fun holidays, too. At Chinese New Year, homes are decorated with red paper. Children get red envelopes for good luck. What do you like best about winter? Your friend, Annie

passage.title: Spring
passage.text: Dear Kindergartners, After winter, the next season is spring! Spring includes March, April, and May. The days get longer, and the air gets warmer. The snow and ice begin to thaw. Animals wake up from their long winter sleep. Spring is a very windy season. It is a perfect time to fly a kite! There are many rainy days, too. I love to splash in puddles in my rain boots. After the rain, you may see a rainbow in the sky. In April, the cherry trees in my city are full of pink and white blossoms. On farms, farmers plant seeds in neat rows. Soon, little green seedlings come up. What is spring like where you live? Your friend, Annie

passage.title: Summer
passage.text: Dear Kindergartners, Today I will tell you about summer. Summer includes June, July, and August. The days are the longest of the year. Summer is the hottest season. When it is hot, the liquid in the thermometer goes up high. Summer is my favorite season because I love the warm sunshine. There is no school, so it is vacation time! I like to swim at the pool to keep cool. I wear sunscreen so I do not get a sunburn. On the hottest days, some people rest in the shade or stay indoors. The Fourth of July is the birthday of the United States. At night, we watch colorful fireworks. What is summer like where you live? Your friend, Annie

passage.title: Autumn
passage.text: Dear Kindergartners, After summer comes autumn, and kids go back to school. Autumn includes September, October, and November. The air gets cooler, and there is a chill at night. The days get shorter and shorter. The leaves on many trees turn yellow, orange, red, and brown. Then the trees shed their leaves. That is why autumn is also called fall! We rake the leaves into a big pile and jump in it. Autumn is harvest time on farms. Farmers pick the fruits and vegetables that grew all summer. At the county fair, I saw giant pumpkins. In November, my family eats Thanksgiving dinner together. Soon it will be winter, and the cycle of the seasons starts again. Your friend, Annie

tasks.title: Read: The Grasshopper and the Ants

passage.title: The Grasshopper and the Ants
passage.text: On a fine summer day, a grasshopper hopped in a field. He sang and danced all day long. Nearby, the ants worked hard. They filled their house with food for the long, cold winter. The grasshopper said, “Come and play with me!” But the ants kept working. Then autumn came, and the leaves fell from the trees. Soon it was winter. The grasshopper was cold and hungry. He knocked on the ants' door and asked, “May I share your food?” The ants asked, “What did you do all summer?” The grasshopper said, “I sang and danced in the sun.” As he walked away, he sang, “Next time I'll work as well as dance. Then I'll be ready, like the ants!”

passage.title: Safety in Storms
passage.text: Dear Kindergartners, Today I will tell you how to stay safe in a thunderstorm. Big, dark clouds mean a storm is coming. During a thunderstorm, lightning flashes in the sky. Then you hear a loud clap of thunder. Thunder cannot hurt you, but lightning can. Lightning likes to strike tall things, like trees. So the best place to be in a storm is indoors. A car is safe, too. Never stand under a tree in a storm! If you are in a pool, get out right away. Sometimes a storm brings hail. Hail is little balls of ice that fall from the clouds. If you must go out in the rain, wear the right gear: a raincoat, boots, and a hat. Your friend, Annie

passage.title: Meteorology
passage.text: Dear Kindergartners, This is my last letter about seasons and weather. A meteorologist is a person who studies the weather. Meteorologists try to predict, or guess, what the weather will be like tomorrow. This helps people know what to wear. Will you need an umbrella or sunscreen? Farmers need to know when it will rain, too. Satellites high up in space take pictures of the clouds. The pictures help meteorologists see storms coming. You can look at the clouds, too! White, puffy clouds mean nice weather. Big, dark clouds may bring a storm. Meteorologists also warn people when a big storm is on the way. Thank you for helping me with my weather project! Your friend, Annie
